theorem: Let R_w be any nonnegative diagonal weighted source-grid operator defined below. Assume alpha,beta,epsilon,phi,eta,iota>0, beta*delta>=alpha^2, and with K2=alpha^3/beta^2 assume K2*(1/epsilon+alpha/(phi*iota))<=1 and phi*eta>=K2*epsilon. Then EVERY rank-four Bob map with kernel in span{|0>,|2>,|3>} has an output with Schmidt number <=2, for all complex kernel coefficients. No PPT hypothesis is needed for this sufficient SR2 conclusion. Whenever R_w is PPT, its projection is an actual 4x4 PPT state with SN<=2. This extends the fixed-weight entire-plane result to a nontrivial continuous weighted source family, not all 4x4 PPT states.
weighted_source: Use [q]=|q><q|, A=|00>+|11>+|22>, B=|01>+|12>, D=|10>-|21>, C=|02>+|34>, E=|20>+|33>, F=|23>, G=|30>, I=|32>, H=|04>, and R_w=alpha[A]+beta[B]+delta[D]+gamma[C]+epsilon[E]+phi[F]+eta[G]+iota[I]+kappa[H] with all weights nonnegative. The specified range is the Krebs–Gachechiladze 4x5 grid https://arxiv.org/html/2509.07086v1 Eq.11; the corrected exact range/SN3 argument is in frontier-20261028-grid-state-five-projections-v1.json SHA256 9863760e2ca2331164d12e62300f3ad7db5b6a17a3ef424e360d504d541004a9.
map_and_notation: For a kernel in the plane with nonzero |3> coordinate, after an invertible output map take K|0,1,2>=|0,1,2>, K|3>=v0|0>+v2|2>, K|4>=|3>. Write U=|v0|^2,V=|v2|^2; primes denote images. E'=|20>+v0|30>+v2|32>, F'=v0|20>+v2|22>, G'=|30>, I'=|32>, C'=|02>+|33>, H'=|03>, and X=E'-v0G'-v2I'=|20>. Set delta0=alpha^2/beta<=delta, k=sqrt(alpha^3)/beta>0, k^2=K2.
first_exact_decomposition: Set Cw=1/epsilon+U/eta+V/iota and s=-Cw*phi*k*conjugate(v0)/(1+Cw*phi*U). Put W=-kX+s(F'-v0X). For each z^4=1, q_z=sqrt(alpha)*z*A'+sqrt(beta)*B'+(alpha/sqrt(beta))*z^2*D'+z^3*W has SR<=2: its upper 3x3 determinant is z^3*(alpha^(3/2)-beta*k)=0, because the e22 cofactor alpha-sqrt(beta)*(alpha/sqrt(beta)) vanishes. The phase average is alpha[A']+beta[B']+delta0[D']+[W]. The residual is (delta-delta0)[D']+gamma[C']+kappa[H'] plus a Gram H1=diag(epsilon,eta,iota,phi)-t1*t1^* over (E',G',I',F'), with t1=(-(k+s*v0),(k+s*v0)*v0,(k+s*v0)*v2,s). Every vector in this four-generator span has Alice support only on rows2,3. Exact Schur minimization shows H1>=0 iff Cw*K2/(1+Cw*phi*U)<=1 for this optimized s, i.e. Cw*(K2-phi*U)<=1.
second_exact_decomposition: For V>0 set Z=|22>=(F'-v0E'+v0^2G'+v0*v2 I')/v2. Let q0=sqrt(alpha)*(A'-Z) and, for z^4=1, q_z=sqrt(alpha)*z*(A'+Z)+sqrt(2*beta)*z^2*B'+(sqrt(2)*alpha/sqrt(beta))*D'. All have SR<=2: the upper determinant of q_z is sqrt(alpha)*z^3*(2*alpha-sqrt(2*beta)*(sqrt(2)*alpha/sqrt(beta)))=0, and q0 uses only the first two diagonal slots. Their mixture (1/2)[q0]+(1/8)sum[q_z] equals alpha[A']+beta[B']+delta0[D']+alpha[Z]. The remaining operator has the same nonnegative D',C',H' terms and Gram H2=diag(epsilon,eta,iota,phi)-alpha*t2*t2^*, with t2=(-v0/v2,v0^2/v2,v0,1/v2). It is PSD iff alpha*(U/(V*epsilon)+U^2/(V*eta)+U/iota+1/(V*phi))<=1.
exhaustion_proof: If U>=K2/phi, the first Gram condition holds for every V because K2-phi*U<=0. Otherwise set m=K2-phi*U>0 and A0=1/epsilon+U/eta. The first Gram covers V<=V1=iota*(1/m-A0). The second covers V>=V2=alpha*(U*A0+1/phi)/(1-alpha*U/iota). The denominator is positive: K2*(1/epsilon+alpha/(phi*iota))<=1 and K2/epsilon>0 imply alpha*K2/(phi*iota)<1, hence alpha*U<iota. Direct subtraction shows V1>=V2 exactly when 1-K2/epsilon-alpha*K2/(phi*iota)+U*(phi/epsilon-K2/eta)+(phi/eta)*U^2>=0. Its constant term is nonnegative by the first weight assumption, its linear coefficient by phi*eta>=K2*epsilon, and its quadratic coefficient is positive. Thus [0,V1] and [V2,infinity) cover all V>=0, with V2>0. The first branch covers V=0. At the projective boundary where the |3> kernel coefficient is zero, the kernel lies in span{|0>,|2>}; then A' itself has SR<=2 and every original generator already has SR<=2, so the original nonnegative weighted sum suffices. Any surjective map with that kernel differs by an invertible output filter.
explicit_ppt_sn3_source: For weights (alpha,beta,delta,gamma,epsilon,phi,eta,iota,kappa)=(1,1,2,3,9,9,9,6,7), K2=1, the required inequalities read 1/9+1/54=7/54<1 and 81>=9. An exact 20x20 partial-transpose pivot calculation proves R_w PPT; its trace is 64. Every weight is positive, so its range is the same 9-dimensional source-grid range. The cited corrected minor identity shows all SR<=2 vectors in this range have A-coefficient zero, whereas A occurs with positive weight. Therefore R_w/64 has SN>=3; its defining decomposition has ranks <=3, so SN=3 exactly. For EVERY kernel in the full CP^2 plane its actual 4x4 projection is PPT/SN<=2 by the theorem. This example is not a 4x4 SN>=3 candidate.

sample_exact_check.observed: At the stated weighted PPT/SN3 source and v0=1/2,v2=4, two independent 256-entry reconstruction checks pass; all nine phase vectors have rank<=2. First Gram has Cw=101/36, s=-202/117, optimized cost 404/1053, with positive exact pivots; second Gram cost=13/256 with positive exact pivots. Both the actual 16x16 projected PT and the 20x20 source PT have nonnegative Gaussian-rational Schur pivots. The checker hash-pins and replays five prior unweighted cases. An initial sample with epsilon=6 failed its source and output PPT pivot checks; increasing epsilon to9 and rerunning produced the stated success. The failed sample is not claimed PPT.

limits: The sufficient weight inequalities define a proper family. Arbitrary weighted grid states, other 3-support planes without separately transformed weight conditions, generic CP^4 kernels, unrestricted 4x4 PPT states, novelty, and external/formal review remain open.
